The Excalidraw style gives any vector entity a hand-drawn whiteboard look: a wobbled, pen-like outline plus optional hachure-style fills. It lives in [`src/engine/style/excalidraw`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/style/excalidraw).

cells.text: Static facade: `apply`, `setTime`, `getTime`, `setSeed`, `boil`, `createAnim`, `startBoil`, `stopBoil`, `isBoiling`; manages per-entity option memory.
Fluent method on any `VectorEntity` (Rect, Circle, Path, Arrow, SVG, etc.) applying hand-drawn whiteboard styling.
Fluent shortcuts to start and stop continuous background line-boil.
Composite animation drawing shape contours and fills while simultaneously boiling lines.
First-class `Animation` for timeline-based 12 FPS organic sketch boil.
`WobbleModifier` applying biomechanical wrist bowing, motor tremor, passes, and corner overshoot.
Polygon clipping and scanline raycasting generating fill pattern contours.
SplitMix32/Murmur3 finalizer hashing entity IDs into deterministic seeds.

blocks.text: Every Excalidraw shape uses pseudo-random jitter. The seed system is controlled entirely through the `seed` option:

items: When set to `'auto'` (the default in `DEFAULT_EXCALIDRAW_OPTIONS`), each path deterministically derives its seed from its `entity.id` via `seedFromEntityId(path.id)` using a 32-bit SplitMix32 finalizer.
**Why it matters:** Distinct shapes in a diagram automatically look uniquely hand-drawn without requiring the user to assign unique seeds manually.

**Scene Determinism:** Entity sequence numbers (`Entity.seq_no`) are automatically reset on scene reload (`Scene.reset()` and Studio HMR), guaranteeing that shapes always produce identical jitter across browser refreshes and video render passes.
When a numeric seed is provided (e.g., `seed: 505`), the shape uses that exact seed regardless of its entity ID.
Useful when a specific artistic sketch contour or corner overshoot is desired.
**`Excalidraw.setSeed(entity, seed)`**: Re-styles the entity with a new seed while preserving all previous colors, stroke widths, and fill options.
**`entity.toExcalidraw({ seed })`**: Equivalent chainable method on any `VectorEntity`.

blocks.text: To prevent z-fighting and ensure clean visual hierarchies, Excalidraw separates the outline, hatching lines, and wash fill across calibrated z-planes:

items: **Top Plane (`z = 0.00`) — Outline Stroke:** Crisp hand-drawn border and corners.
**Middle Plane (`z = -0.01`, `FILL_Z`) — Hatch Lines:** Hand-drawn diagonal, cross-hatch, or zigzag fill lines.
**Bottom Plane (`z = -0.02`, `WASH_Z`) — Translucent Wash:** Soft background wash fill, letting the card's backdrop or canvas show through without obscuring the hatch lines.

blocks.text: 4. Line-Boil Animation System: setSeed vs setTime
Understanding the difference between `setSeed` and `setTime` is critical for performance and animation:

cells.text: Changes the shape's static hand-drawn blueprint/ID.
Drives the continuous 12 FPS line boil (wobble) over time.
**Full Scene Graph Rebuild:** Destroys previous child paths, re-evaluates polygon clipping in `HachureGenerator`, re-allocates new `Path` nodes, and re-binds GPU vertex buffers.
**Lightweight Property Update:** Only updates `.time` on the existing `ExcalidrawModifier`s. Never destroys paths, never re-clips polygons.
Blazing fast (0 allocations, sub-millisecond, runs at 60–120 FPS).
Initial construction, or switching static variations.

blocks.text: The Built-in Boil Animation: boilAnim() / entity.boil()
To animate line-boil on the timeline without writing manual `CustomAnimation` boilerplate, use the built-in animation helpers:
Inside `BoilAnimation`, time is smoothly advanced and quantized to 12 FPS (`boilFps`), matching the traditional cel animation wobble of whiteboard hand-drawn sketches.
To draw shape outlines and fills while boiling sketch lines simultaneously:

`Excalidraw.createAnim` wraps the inner `createAnim` and `BoilAnimation` inside a parallel `Concurrent` (`lagRatio: 0.0`), isolating boiling to run continuously across the entire duration while delegating `stagger` and `distribution` to the inner path creation sequence. Geometric arc lengths are computed synchronously from path vertex contours.
When whiteboard diagrams should boil continuously in the background across animations and holds:

Under the hood, continuous boiling is powered by Retiam's native `entity.always()` loop and tracked with a private `WeakMap`. It introduces zero memory leaks and automatically cancels when the entity is disposed or destroyed.

items: **Geometry:** `ExcalidrawModifier` (subclass of `WobbleModifier`) adds tremor (`roughness`), wrist arc (`bowing`), a second overlapping pass (`passes: 2`, bowing the same direction as the first so the two strokes read as one natural retraced line), corner `overshoot`, and optional `crossCorners` for architectural boxes.
**Passes & Solid Fills:** Paths with solid fills (e.g. arrowheads) use a single pass (`passes: 1`) because two overlapping loops would cancel each other out under even-odd winding rules.

**Shader:** Integrated felt-tip [`PathEffect.Sketch`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/material/path_effects/SketchEffect.ts) dynamics with organic pressure variations. Closed contours use seamless circular noise to eliminate corner discontinuities; open contours (arrows, lines) apply tapering start and end pressure ramps. Pass `strokeShader: null` for a uniform-width line.

blocks.text: Fills are created when `fillColor` is specified:

cells.text: Parallel diagonal strokes at `fillAngle`, spaced by `fillGap`.
Two intersecting sets of angled strokes forming a diagonal mesh grid.
Orthogonal horizontal (0°) and vertical (90°) perpendicular cross grid.
Continuous back-and-forth zigzag stroke with curved boundary turns.
Expressive continuous marker scribble with organic looping Bézier turns and motor tremor.
Stippled dot field; point count is capped for high rendering performance.
Opaque solid color fill with hand-drawn edge contouring.

blocks.text: Fills include an optional translucent background wash (`fillBackground: true`, default `alpha: 0.40`), allowing cards to have both soft tinting and crisp hatch lines. Set `fillBackground: false` for pure hand-drawn marker or grid strokes with the canvas showing through.
